title: Handle a capability gap as a typed error
prompt: Write a standalone TypeScript ESM program that demonstrates Honua's fail-closed capability contract. Build a WFS source with the contract API from @honua/sdk-js: HonuaClient with { baseUrl: <HONUA_EVAL_BASE_URL> }, createDataset from @honua/sdk-js/contract with one source { id: "countries", protocol: "wfs", locator: { url: <base URL>/geoserver/ows, typeName: "ne:ne_10m_admin_0_countries" }, capabilities: PROTOCOL_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES.wfs } and skipCompatibilityCheck: true. Then call source.queryAggregate({ aggregation: { groupBy: [], metrics: [{ fn: "count", field: "OBJECTID", alias: "n" }] } }) inside try/catch. WFS does not support server-side aggregation, so the SDK must throw HonuaCapabilityNotSupportedError (exported from @honua/sdk-js) instead of returning empty data. Print exactly one line to stdout: {"caught": <true when the caught error is an instanceof HonuaCapabilityNotSupportedError>, "capability": <the error's capability property>, "errorName": <the error's name>}.

context.notes: Golden workflow: capability gaps throw HonuaCapabilityNotSupportedError; agents must branch on the typed error.
